conviction_note: Near-zero net: the one genuinely stale company-stated number I found (a 15% back-half tariff assumption superseded by the 10%/12.5% Section 301 regime that took effect 2026-07-24) is worth roughly +2, and it is offset by the 2Q26 retail base rate that the market strips IEEPA refunds out of headline beats and by an incoming CFO delivering his first call on a plan requiring 81% of the year's operating income in the back half; against a 13.33% implied move I have nothing that justifies more than a low-single-digit tilt.

findings.finding: AEO's fiscal 2026 guidance is built on 'a tariff rate of 10% for second quarter receipts and 15% for the back-half of the fiscal year' (set 2026-05-28, reaffirmed 2026-07-01), but the Section 122 10% surcharge expired at its 150-day limit on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same day by a Section 301 forced-labor tariff of 10% base / 12.5% for a 46-economy higher tier that includes Vietnam, China and Thailand — so AEO's actual blended back-half rate on a Vietnam/Bangladesh/India/Cambodia/Indonesia sourcing base is roughly 10.5-12%, not 15%, and the company has not publicly revised the assumption since the regime changed.
findings.why_not_priced: The preview literature is still quoting the 15% back-half rate as fact and framing it as the central risk — a 2026-09-08 preview is titled 'American Eagle Needs 81% Of Its Year In The Back Half — While The Tariff Rate Steps Up' and builds its whole bear case on the 10%-to-15% step-up, one day before the print. If the market had reconciled AEO's May assumption against the July 24 statutory replacement, that preview could not have been written that way, the 25-delta skew would not be +6.6 puts-bid, and the stock would not be trading 38.9% below its 52-week high on a plan whose largest stated cost headwind is roughly 3-4 points of receipt value lighter than budgeted. AEO set the number before the regime existed and reaffirmed it on 2026-07-01, three weeks before the change.
findings.independence: Independent confirmation of the same regime change from a different publisher: https://www.tariffstool.com/tariffs-from-vietnam (last updated 2026-08-24) states Vietnam is 12.5% under the Section 301 forced-labor tariff effective 2026-07-24, replacing Section 122. The company-side anchor is a separate document, https://www.aeo-inc.com/2026/05/28/american-eagle-outfitters-reports-first-quarter-results-5/ (2026-05-28), whose guidance footnote states the 10%/15% assumption.

findings.finding: AEO will report GAAP EPS several times the $0.21 consensus purely mechanically — it told CNBC on 2026-06-03 it had already received $108m of IEEPA refunds, its 10-Q says the amount plus any further refunds will be recorded as a reduction of cost of sales for the 13 weeks ending 2026-08-01, and guidance explicitly excludes it — but the 2Q26 retail season's own base rate is that the market strips these out: Kohl's fell about 6% on a $150m refund and a raised full-year outlook, Target's stock fell on a beat containing $1.65/share of refund, and the only large positive reaction (ANF +36%) came with a 23% underlying beat ex-refund.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a correction to a mispricing of the *reaction function*, not of the fact. AEO's own tape shows the read-across is unresolved: the stock rose 5.14% on 2026-08-26 (ANF's refund-driven print) and gave back 5.12% on 2026-08-27, a clean round trip to zero, and the 20-day run-up is -0.78%. That pattern is what an unsettled question looks like, not a priced one. If the market had settled it in the bullish direction the run-up would be positive and the skew would be call-bid; if it had settled it bearishly there would be no 5% up-day. The consequence is that the near-certain 3x headline beat is not the catalyst a naive reading of the six-estimate consensus implies, and the resulting full-year operating-income raise from ~$390-410m to ~$500m+ will be discounted as a non-recurring item that has to be lapped in 2027.
findings.independence: Coresight's 2026-09-08 survey of 2Q26 refund bookings and the guidance split across Walmart, Target, TJX, Ross, Dollar Tree, Dollar General, Lululemon, Deckers, Crocs and Levi's points the same way from a different publisher: https://coresight.com/research/tariff-refunds-in-2q26-billions-booked-by-retailers-and-brands-guidance-split/ . The AEO-specific refund fact is from a separate source again, https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/06/03/american-eagle-outfitters-says-it-has-received-108-million-in-tariff-refunds-so-far.html (2026-06-03).

findings.finding: Ravi Thanawala became AEO's CFO effective 2026-08-03 — two days after the quarter being reported closed on 2026-08-01 — succeeding Mike Mathias after 25 years, and tonight is his first earnings call; he inherits, without having set it, a full-year plan whose arithmetic requires $324.5m of the $390-410m operating-income guide (81.1%) to land in the back half, a 4.3x ramp off $75.5m of first-half operating income.
findings.why_not_priced: The CFO change was covered as a personnel story in early July and has not been connected to the shape of the guide it lands on top of. Every preview I found — including the 2026-09-08 one that does the 81.1% arithmetic — treats the back-half loading as a pure operating question and does not mention that the person who now owns that number started 37 days ago and did not build it. If the market had connected them, the coverage would frame tonight as a rebasing event rather than a beat-or-miss on $0.21, and a stock 38.9% off its high with a plan needing a 4.3x second-half ramp would carry more than a 6.6-point 25-delta skew on 188% ATM implied vol, which is proportionally flat for an event of this kind. Note the offset that is genuinely priced: the company reaffirmed both Q2 and full-year guidance in this same release on 2026-07-01, which caps how bad the Q2 underlying can plausibly be.
findings.independence: The 81.1% back-half arithmetic is from a different source and a different date: https://tradesandgains.substack.com/p/american-eagle-needs-81-of-its-year (2026-09-08), which computes $75.5m first-half versus $324.5m implied second-half operating income. Peer evidence that the back-half consumer is not obliging is separate again — ANF's Hollister comps -3% and Gap comps -1% over the identical weeks (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/26/3351233/0/en/abercrombie-fitch-co-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results.html, 2026-08-26). This finding shares the May 28 guidance document as background with finding 1, but rests on a different primary document (the July 1 8-K exhibit) and cuts the opposite way.

searched_and_found_nothing: BofA's reinstatement at Underperform with a $16 price objective, citing Bloomberg Second Measure data showing American Eagle brand sales -15% year over year in the week ending August 2 against Aerie +12% and OFFLINE +29% — the only URL I could reach for it (https://www.thestreet.com/retail/american-eagle-stock-bofa-aerie-growth-retail-clothes-shopping-change) returned HTTP 403 and carries no year in its path, and I could not confirm from the document itself whether it is August 2026 or August 2025. Dropped rather than used, because the datapoint would also need disentangling from the Sydney Sweeney launch week of 2025-07-23 to 2025-08-02, which sits in the last ten days of the year-ago comparison quarter.

Any new or increased share repurchase authorisation announced ahead of the print — ANF's +36% was attributed partly to a raised buyback target and AEO now holds roughly $126m of unexpected refund cash against a $2.9bn cap, but I found no 8-K or release announcing one, so it stays speculation.
Placer.ai or any other foot-traffic panel for AE and Aerie mall doors across May-July 2026 — no accessible dated series.
Any AEO management appearance, conference presentation or public update between the 2026-07-01 guidance reaffirmation and tonight that would refresh the quarter-to-date picture.

A September 2026 executive order changing apparel tariff rates — the 'September 5 / Annex III / Vietnam 20% reciprocal' result that search surfaced resolves to Executive Order 14346 of 2025-09-05, an IEEPA measure struck down in February 2026, not a current 2026 action.
The company's own Q2 10-Q for the period ended 2026-08-01 — not yet filed, so the final refund figure booked to cost of sales above the $108.3m already disclosed is unknown.

Insider signal: Form 4 clusters on 2026-07-06, 2026-07-09 and 2026-07-28 plus a Form 3 on 2026-08-05, but EDGAR's browse interface would not return reporting-owner names, so I could not tell routine vesting from a directional cluster.

The baseline's own history block is empty and wrong for a reason worth recording: EDGAR shows a former-name record with an end date of 2026-08-05 for 'American Eagle Outfitters Inc' to the identical current name, which caused the baseline code to discard all 30 prior prints as a predecessor entity. There is no predecessor — it is a cosmetic registrant-name refresh, and AEO's real reaction history is intact but unavailable to me in the sealed file.
baseline_tension: Mostly cuts with the baseline rather than against it — my two negatives agree with the +6.6 puts-bid skew and the -38.9% drawdown, which is exactly the pattern the brief warns is already priced, and the one finding that genuinely cuts against the skew (a stale 15% back-half tariff assumption superseded on 2026-07-24) is not large enough to flip the net, which is why the number is small.
